I will keep it simple and low-risk. In Quzhou County, the crop I trust most is the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I know this system, I can manage it with machinery, the market is stable, and I do not need to gamble on a complicated cash crop. At 47, with the kind of labor and energy I realistically have, I would rather run a familiar grain rotation well than spread myself thin.

So this year I will put my land into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 30 mu. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed, not old local seed and not an expensive high-risk arrangement. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive nitrogen, because too much only raises cost and can cause lodging or waste. I will plough before wheat when needed to deal with straw and improve the seedbed, then manage weeds and disease with a few targeted sprays, and irrigate at the key water periods. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize with hybrid seed, keep the stand uniform, use rotary tillage for fast turnaround, apply fertilizer in a tighter way, and irrigate mainly at the critical stages if rainfall is short. My goal is steady yield, controlled cost, and no unnecessary risk.
